fairness.flags: FUSE_RESADD constexpr selects the epilogue; unfused = the same kernel with the flag off plus epilogue_kernel(HAS_RES=True)
fairness.protocol: Both arms search the SAME coarse grid object, then each refines around its own winner, then each gets a stage-3 pass of the same size: joint GEMMxEpilogue where the side has an epilogue, extra GEMM neighbours where it does not (a SPLIT_K==1 fused chain has none). No config is ever shared. Every config is checked against the fp32 reference before it is timed.
fairness.layout: B is [K,N] contiguous; identical tensor for triton and vendor.
fairness.split_k: SPLIT_K>1 accumulates into an fp32 buffer with tl.atomic_add, so the chain is [zero, gemm, epilogue]. Both sides pay that identically; the fused epilogue is a cast, the unfused one is cast+add.

tma.evidence: hopper.caps().tma=True (source preflight); preflight probe tma_tensor_descriptor=False -- LIVE PROBE WINS: the preflight probe for this axis is inconclusive

h200_axes.generic_overlays: none at module scope (overlays are per kernel module; see per_family)
h200_axes.policy: every offered axis is applied to the coarse grid of BOTH arms; per-arm live counts are under grids.<regime>.<arm>.<stage>.axis_counts

selection.note: no --gpu given; the process sees whatever devices it inherited. On a multi-tenant host that is how a contended GPU gets measured -- see the preflight's 40 us harness floor.

timing.protocol: final per-regime timings are A/B interleaved within one loop with the order alternating each round; the reported speedup is the median of the per-round ratios, so monotone drift cancels
